methodological_eligibility.evidence_quote: This paper focuses on the framework of reference for Comprehensive Risk Management CRM

stage1.ineligibility_reason: Presents a comprehensive risk/opportunity (R/O) management framework (CMS QHSE3+) in which energy efficiency (E2) is one component addressed via ISO 50001 best practices and risk-vulnerability reduction. EnPI and EnB are mentioned only incidentally within the ISO 50001 context; no EnPI/EnB measurement model is identified or characterised (no variables, functional form, or construction/estimation approach). The only quantitative model characterised is the vulnerability-reduction metric %DismVul (possibility x gravity), a risk metric, not an energy performance model; reported energy results are per-capita consumption-reduction percentages, not a charted EnPI/EnB model.

paper_type.evidence_quote: a Reference Framework for Comprehensive Risk Management (CRM)

stage1.notes: Energy efficiency treated as a risk/vulnerability component under ISO 50001; per-capita consumption-reduction KPIs reported, but no EnPI/EnB model is constructed or characterised.
